us_nonfuel_import_price_to_broad_dollar.description: Cumulative response of the US-dollar non-fuel import price index to a 1.0 permanent depreciation of the broad dollar (so 10% appreciation lowers the index by 10 x value)

long_run.source: Campa-Goldberg (WP 2002) 0.41; Gopinath 2015 0.44 (8 quarters); Burstein-Gopinath 2014 0.51; Fed USIT note 2016 about 0.30 (elasticity of core import prices ~0.3)

monthly_speed_to_long_run.source: median price duration 11 months in dollar prices (Gopinath-Rigobon 2007; GIR 2010); existing master value 0.08 (config import_pass_through_speed)

us_nonfuel_import_price_to_broad_dollar.model_check: master config import_pass_through_long 0.45 with speed 0.08 gives 0.10 at 3m, 0.28 at 12m, 0.39 at 24m: within the range above; keep

long_run.source: GIR 2010: rises above 50% in the long run

us_import_price_from_bloc_formula.formula: Gamma_j(h) = theta_j * G_usd(h) + (1 - theta_j) * G_nonusd(h): response of the USD import price from bloc j to a 1.0 depreciation of j's currency against the dollar. G_usd = 0.24 at 12 months and 0.47 long run (dollar-priced goods, adjusting at 0.08 per month); G_nonusd = 0.90 at 12 months and 0.95 long run (adjusts within 1-2 months)
us_import_price_from_bloc_formula.check: the import-weighted 12-month value should match the aggregate 0.22-0.34 (Cavallo et al. 2021 0.22; Gopinath 2015 0.34-0.44; own LP manufactured 0.21-0.25)

conversion_rules.annual_to_monthly_flow: divide annual level by 12; do not seasonally adjust sector shares
conversion_rules.quarterly_to_monthly_speed: monthly speed m = 1 - (1 - q)^(1/3) from a quarterly closing share q
conversion_rules.partial_adjustment_form: z_t = z_{t-1} + lambda (x_t - z_{t-1});  ln f_t = -eps_SR x_t - (eps_LR - eps_SR) z_t  (same form as b7-tariff M2)
conversion_rules.income_effect_timing: apply the income elasticity to the three-month moving average of bloc GDP growth: income effects are felt mostly contemporaneously (Fed USIT note 2016)

recommended_rule.form: tau*_{j,s,t} = min(cap_j, kappa_j * w_s * max_{k=0..ell_j} tau_US->j,t-k); tau*_t = tau*_{t-1} + mu (target - tau*_{t-1}), mu_up = 1, mu_down = 0.1 (ratchet)

CN.unit: ratio of partner's average duty to US average duty on that partner

CA.source: 2025: 25% on C$30bn (4 Mar) and C$14.2bn (13 Mar) of US goods, removed 1 Sep 2025 except steel/aluminium/autos (Canada Dept of Finance; Blakes)

EU.source: 2025: countermeasures adopted 24 Jul to apply from 7 Aug, then suspended 5 Aug 2025 for six months; 2018: 25% on about $3.5bn of US imports (Bown, PIIE 2018)

MX.source: no tariff retaliation in 2025 (unverified here); 2018 retaliated on pork, steel, cheese

IN.source: 2018-19: delayed retaliation on 28 products; 2025: none found

UK.source: OWNER CHOICE (proxy for the euro area, 2026-10-15): the UK retaliates like the EU (kappa 0.2, range 0.0-0.6, lag 2 months). Evidence: 2018, the UK was inside the EU rebalancing (25% on about $3.5bn of US imports, Bown PIIE 2018); 2025, the UK consulted on a list of US goods to target (April 2025) but agreed the US-UK deal (May 2025) and applied no duties. So this is a modelling choice, not a measured 2025 response.
